I designed 100 experiments as 10 groups. Each group applies one fixed edit to 10 parents that differ in their other edges, so the same edit's effect can be compared across conditions:

| Edit | Main conditions it probes |
|---|---|
| edge 5 → none | Whether edge 3 (the input→output edge) is skip, none or a conv |
| edge 3 → skip | Whether it replaces none or a conv; whether the paths through edges 4 and 5 are present |
| edge 3 → none | Same as above, removing instead of adding |
| edge 0 → nor_conv_3x3 | Whether edges 2 and 4 (the ones using node 1) are none |
| edge 0 → none | Same as above |
| edge 1 → nor_conv_3x3 | Whether edge 5 (node 2 → output) is present |
| edge 2 → skip | What node 1 computes and whether edge 5 exists |
| edge 4 → avg_pool_3x3 | Which op it replaces; whether edge 3 is skip |
| edge 4 → none | Same as above |
| edge 5 → nor_conv_3x3 | Which op it replaces; whether edge 3 is skip |

The parents mix 16 cells, from all-conv cells to sparse cells with pooling. No experiment is a no-op: each parent's current op on the edited edge differs from the new op. My helper script's printed output was inconsistent, so I didn't use it. I built and checked the list below by hand.
